rules.title: Application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: An application screening fee may not exceed the landlord's actual out-of-pocket costs of gathering information on the applicant. In no case may it exceed thirty dollars ($30) per applicant, which may be adjusted annually with increases in the Consumer Price Index beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.key_value: Actual out-of-pocket costs, not more than $30 per applicant, adjustable annually by CPI beginning January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who charge applicants, including guarantors or cosignors, an application screening fee to rent residential property.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.
rules.interaction_text: The application screening fee shall not be considered an “advance fee” as that term is used in Section 10026 of the Business and Professions Code, and shall not be considered “security” as that term is used in Section 1950.5.

rules.title: No screening fee when no unit is available
rules.requirement: A landlord or their agent may not charge an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents charging application screening fees.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent shall not charge an applicant an application screening fee when they know or should have known that no rental unit is available at that time or will be available within a reasonable period of time.

rules.title: Required screening process to charge a fee (first-qualified or refund)
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge a screening fee only if, when the fee is collected, it offers either a process considering completed applications in order received with written criteria, approving the first qualifying applicant and charging only applicants actually considered (refunding within seven days fees inadvertently collected from unconsidered applicants), or a process returning the entire fee to any applicant not selected within 7 days of selecting a tenant or 30 days of application submission, whichever occurs first.
rules.key_value: Refund within 7 days of selecting an applicant or 30 days of submission, whichever occurs first
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents charging application screening fees.
rules.exemptions: Under the first-in-order process, no refund is required to an applicant whose application is denied after consideration because the applicant does not meet the landlord's established screening criteria; the landlord may instead offer, at the applicant's discretion, to apply the fee to another rental unit offered by the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord or their agent may charge an applicant an application screening fee only if the landlord or their agent, at the time the application screening fee is collected, offers any of the following:

rules.title: Itemized receipt and refund of unused screening fee
rules.requirement: The landlord or agent must give the applicant a receipt, personally or by mail (or by email if agreed), itemizing out-of-pocket expenses and time spent obtaining and processing the applicant's information. If no personal reference check or consumer credit report is obtained, any unused portion of the fee must be returned to the applicant.
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who collect an application screening fee.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord or their agent shall provide, personally, or by mail, the applicant with a receipt for the fee paid by the applicant, which receipt shall itemize the out-of-pocket expenses and time spent by the landlord or their agent to obtain and process the information about the applicant.

rules.title: Copy of consumer credit report to fee-paying applicant
rules.requirement: If an applicant has paid a screening fee, the landlord or agent must provide the applicant a copy of their consumer credit report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of receiving it.
rules.key_value: within seven days of receiving the report
rules.coverage_text: Landlords (owners of residential rental property) or their agents who have collected an application screening fee and obtained a consumer credit report.
rules.quoted_span: If an application screening fee has been paid by the applicant, the landlord or their agent shall provide a copy of the consumer credit report to the applicant who is the subject of that report by personal delivery, mail, or email within seven days of the landlord or their agent receiving the report.
